title: Memphis printed cotton swatch card
lede: A sample card of Memphis printed cottons under a black header with the group’s blocky wordmark.
summary: 1985 Memphis swatch: tilted turquoise squares on red under a MEMPHIS header card.

creator.name: Memphis (designer, as recorded by the V&A)

evidence.note: Downloaded the museum’s published image (843 px wide) from [the V&A IIIF server](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O294419/) to a private scratchpad and inspected it with the Read tool on 2026-09-25. No image is stored in the catalogue. The V&A record gives no pattern title or individual designer.

styles.note: A Memphis trade sample that joins the group’s printed pattern with its graphic identity.

context: The V&A records a swatch of printed cottons, Italy, 1985, with Memphis as designer. [V&A record](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O294419/).
The record does not name the pattern or the designer of the header card.
observed: A black header strip carries “MEMPHIS” in white, squared capitals with cut and notched strokes.
The front swatch shows turquoise squares, tilted at different angles, on a red ground.
Behind it, pinked edges of other fabrics show yellow, orange, and black.
The swatches are fixed to a plain white card with the accession number written below.
interpretation: The letterforms on the header look like Christoph Radl’s 1982 Memphis logotype drawing ([record](ref:radl-memphis-logotype-drawing-1982)). This is a visual comparison; the V&A does not name the designer.
Tilted squares scattered on a strong ground is the simplest version of the Memphis “confetti” pattern.
borrow: Scatter one simple shape at random angles over a contrasting solid ground.
Pair a busy pattern with a black band that carries the brand in heavy white lettering.

rights.statement: The V&A image is credited © Victoria and Albert Museum, London. No image is stored.
